title: Hazel and the Hymn
premise: Hospice nurse Isandro Whitlock has spent her career recording the backwards counts she hears in the final hours of the dying, believing the numbers are a mercy she can document but never stop. When an excavation crew beneath the Holloway estate unearths a door sealed from the inside, the counting spreads to the living: first the groundskeeper, then the family's youngest son, each dying on schedule while Isandro's notebooks fill with their numbers. She discovers the Holloways' fortune was built on a bargain that feeds a chosen family member to whatever waits behind the door, and that the family has quietly chosen her. To break the count, Isandro must lead the surviving Holloways back through the door and offer the ledger of every death she's recorded in place of a life, learning that survival is a debt someone always pays. In the end she seals the door from the inside herself, leaving the family free and her notebooks as the only evidence she ever existed.
about_author: Gideon Dravenmoor spent a decade working night shifts in care facilities across the American Rust Belt before turning to fiction, and his stories trade on the hush of institutions after visiting hours. He lives alone with a filing cabinet of unfinished manuscripts and claims he never writes anything he hasn't already dreamed.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Last Breaths
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the Marrow Creek hospice, she sits with a dying woman who counts backwards from ninety and records it in her ledger, as she has done for eleven years. Her supervisor warns her the notebooks are unprofessional. Emotional beat: the lonely comfort of ritual, and the first hint that Isandro treats documentation as devotion rather than habit.

chapters.title: A House That Outlives Its Name
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She takes a private live-in nursing post at Holloway House, caring for the patriarch Ambrose, whose numbers have already started at an impossibly young age. She meets the fractured family: eldest son Corwin, daughter-in-law Vera, and quiet boy Tennyson. Emotional beat: wary belonging; a found-family shape beginning even as the house feels wrong.

chapters.title: What the Excavator Uncovered
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The crew digging a new wine cellar breaks through to a stone door, sealed from the inside, its hinges fused with something like wax and hair. That night Ambrose's count accelerates. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity, and the sense that the house has been waiting to be opened.

chapters.title: Sealed from Within
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Corwin. Corwin orders the door reburied; Isandro finds tool marks on the inside face and realizes someone once chose to stay. Ambrose dies at zero, smiling, and his count transfers to the groundskeeper Hollis. Emotional beat: grief braided with guilt, and the first proof the count moves between people.

chapters.title: Hollis Counts Down
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She shadows Hollis through his final days, documenting as he deteriorates with eerie serenity, telling her the family 'always pays on time.' She confronts Corwin, who denies everything with rehearsed ease. Emotional beat: the horror of witnessing a scheduled death and being unable to intervene.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Living
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Cross-referencing her old hospice notebooks with the Holloway family Bible, she finds every count she ever recorded traces back through bloodlines to the estate. The pattern is a tithe, one life per generation. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering her whole career was entangled with the house's hunger.

chapters.title: Vera's Quiet Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera reveals she married in knowing the cost, and that the family chooses the tithe by a vote no one speaks aloud. She warns Isandro that this generation's choice has already been made. Emotional beat: complicity and pity; Vera as both victim and enforcer of the system.

chapters.title: Tennyson's Numbers Begin
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Nine-year-old Tennyson starts counting in his sleep, backwards from a number too large for a child's death. Isandro realizes the family voted for the boy, and that the long count means something worse is planned. Emotional beat: protective fury; Isandro's found-family instinct hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: The Vote Nobody Spoke
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. Corwin defends the choice: the tithe bought the family's health, luck, and longevity for a century, and refusing it means everything unravels. He offers Isandro a bribe and a threat in the same breath. Emotional beat: the seduction of power and how easily survival justifies cruelty.

chapters.title: Invisible No Longer
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro discovers her own name in Ambrose's will as 'the Recorder,' a role written generations before she was hired: the family didn't choose Tennyson, they chose her, and the boy's count is bait to keep her close. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into clarity; her invisibility was always the trap.

chapters.title: The Door Remembers Her
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the door, the wax-and-hair seal softens at her touch, and she hears a count in her own voice, backwards, from a number she can't finish hearing. She understands the door wants the Recorder, and always has. Emotional beat: intimate terror; the enemy knows her better than she knows herself.

chapters.title: Running the Count
chapters.summary: Isandro and Tennyson's alternating POV. Isandro flees the estate with Tennyson, whose count drops faster the farther they travel, as if distance feeds the debt. Vera quietly leaves them supplies and a map of the tunnels. Emotional beat: desperate flight and the first real trust between Isandro and the child.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgets
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In Marrow Creek, no one remembers Isandro's eleven years at the hospice; her old records are gone, her references blank. The house edits the world around its debts. Emotional beat: erasure and isolation, the price of being written into someone else's ledger.

chapters.title: Corwin's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. With the tithe fled, Corwin's body begins counting instead, and he realizes the bargain collects from whoever holds the estate's authority. He tries to burn the family Bible; it won't burn. Emotional beat: a powerful man discovering power was only ever a loan.

chapters.title: What Waits Is Patient
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Through the door's seam, Isandro glimpses a corridor of previous Recorders, each frozen mid-count, their notebooks fused to their hands. She recognizes her own handwriting in the oldest. Emotional beat: cosmic horror made personal; she has done this before, or will.

chapters.title: The Bargain Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera breaks generations of silence and reads the founding covenant aloud to Corwin and the household: the door was sealed from the inside by the first Recorder, who traded herself to stop a plague, and every generation since has misunderstood mercy as sacrifice. Emotional beat: revelation reframing everything, sacrifice exposed as a corruption of compassion.

chapters.title: Zero Hour for a Child
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Tennyson's count reaches single digits. Isandro realizes the count can be transferred by consent, not blood, and that her ledger of every recorded death is the only document the door honors. Emotional beat: a race against arithmetic, love weaponized into courage.

chapters.title: The Family That Stayed
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The surviving Holloways gather at the door: Corwin dying, Vera resolute, Tennyson fading. For the first time in a century, the family votes aloud, and votes to give the Recorder whatever she needs. Emotional beat: found family forged in the exact place blood family failed.

chapters.title: The Recorder's Prayer
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro enters the corridor of Recorders and offers her ledger, every count she documented as prayer, as payment in full, demanding the debt close rather than roll forward. The thing behind the door begins counting her backwards. Emotional beat: climax; devotion turned into defiance.

chapters.title: Sealed from the Inside
chapters.summary: Tennyson's POV. Through the closing door, Tennyson watches Isandro take her place among the Recorders, her count ending not at zero but at one, held, unfinished. The door fuses with her hand on the seal, and every count in the house stops. Emotional beat: awe and heartbreak; survival achieved at the cost of the one who paid.

chapters.title: After the Count
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Months later, the Holloways live unremarkably: Tennyson grows, Corwin's health is ordinary, the estate is sold. Vera keeps one of Isandro's blank notebooks and writes in it daily, an accounting no one asked for. Emotional beat: quiet grief and the discipline of remembrance.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Hymn
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Tennyson's POV as an adult. A hospice nurse named Hazel, who hums an old hymn while she works, finds Tennyson's mother's notebook and a single page in Isandro's handwriting: not a count, but a name, his, and the words 'paid in full.' Emotional beat: resolution and echo; the price of survival honored, and documentation, at last, answered.
